title: zForth on DOS (8086) — a tiny libre Forth

components.source: src/zforth/zforth.c + forth/core.zf (zevv/zForth) + dosmain.c (DOS front-end), built with ia16-elf-gcc

toolchain.target: msdos (16-bit MZ .EXE, medium model, newlib + libi86)
toolchain.invocation: ia16-elf-gcc -mcmodel=medium -march=any_186 -O2 -I src/zforth -I src/linux dosmain.c src/zforth/zforth.c -o FORTH.EXE

notes: zForth is a tiny embeddable Forth: a small C VM plus a Forth-source bootstrap (forth/core.zf) that defines the language. dosmain.c embeds core.zf (the language only — the stock misc.zf FizzBuzz demo and memaccess.zf load-time asserts are excluded), evaluates it, prints the banner, then reads PROG.FTH via INT 21h and evaluates it. zf_cell is float, so the build uses the medium model (soft-float %g), like fe-dos. The DOS-native Forth alongside BASIC (ubasic-dos), C (small-c), Lisp (fe-dos) and Tcl (tcl-dos); f83/volksforth are interactive REPLs, zForth is the file-reading Forth that fits PROG.<X>. fetch.sh reproduces FORTH.EXE byte-for-byte.
